The matrix triangle argument is correct for all actions, including nonsymmetric ones; the omission is nonfatal and is repaired by adding the proved corollary as a direct dependency and deriving the unit-vector estimate explicitly in F6.

The symmetric matrix has eigenvectors e1+e2, e1-e2, e3, e4 with eigenvalues 5/4, 3/4, 1, 1. All are positive and at most M=2, and all off-diagonal entries lie in the common size-two block. The Dirac contaminant is Borel probability and epsilon=1/10 is admissible; the mixture supplier applies under inherited AC. Added only the missing dense-class interface and its explicit proof use; Example unchanged.

Checked the clean branch Q=P_Sigma, selection of a loss>omega/2 pair only when omega>M0>=0, the exact TV threshold and epsilon=1 convention, AC-qualified equalization and identical iid sample laws. The triangle inequality for arbitrary matrix actions forces two measurable loss events to cover the sample space; their larger probability is at least 1/2 at a threshold exceeding omega/16. The repaired norm supplier licenses that argument; Statement and action space unchanged.

Checked joint upper semicontinuity with weak-tail ties, finite depth levels, closed cube-hit projections over the compact search class, Borel depth strata and deterministic first-child dyadic selection. The compactness and entry bounds are proved explicitly in the cited supplier, as detailed in the decision. Nested compact fibers yield a unique limit with Borel coordinates. For global selectors, a supported top eigenvector makes every matrix above the data cap have zero depth, and countable Borel pasting gives global maximizers even for zero-depth samples. No item or metadata edit.
